analysis.evidence: הוּא וַעֲבָדָיו identifies Abram and his servants as the group that divided. עֲלֵיהֶם לַיְלָה places the action against their opponents at night, and וַיַּכֵּם then describes Abram striking them.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Niphal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular. The verb precedes its compound subject and agrees with its first member, הוּא.
analysis.sense: Split into groups for an attack.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּחָלֵק עֲלֵיהֶם לַיְלָה, the suffix identifies the enemy against whom Abram and his servants divided their forces at night. The same enemy is the object of וַיַּכֵּם, “he struck them,” and וַיִּרְדְּפֵם, “he pursued them.”
analysis.morphology: The preposition עַל takes the form עֲלֵי־ before the third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix הֶם.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּחָלֵק עֲלֵיהֶם לַיְלָה, לַיְלָה tells when Abram and his servants divided their forces against the enemy.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun used adverbially to indicate time.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers to Abram. After the singular verb וַיֵּחָלֵק, the phrase הוּא וַעֲבָדָיו identifies those who divided up by night: “he and his servants.”
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person masculine singular personal pronoun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: he too; he and his company

analysis.evidence: הוּא וַעֲבָדָיו means “he and his servants.” The phrase identifies Abram and the men of his household who joined him in the night attack.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ means “and.” The noun is masculine plural construct with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.
